messages.subject: Re: effect size statistics
messages.body_plain:
Dear Tobi,

The Bonferroni correction controls family-wise error rate, and is one way to do this. It involves dividing alpha by the number of confidence intervals. Another way is to use the approach by Benjamini and Hochberg, and control False Discovery rate. It is a different adjustment to alpha, see p. 298 of this manuscript http://www.stat.purdue.edu/~doerge/BIOINFORM.D/FALL06/Benjamini%20and%20Y%20FDR.pdf.

For visualization you can make a separate plot per protein (as it is done in MSstats), or overlay all the proteins in one plot.

HTH
Olga

messages.subject: Re: LogOfSum
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

I know this issue. That is because summaryMethod='logOfSum' has different statistical strategy. This option is for repeating what Skyline group comparison. So, it is quite different that what MSstats proposed as default.
1. run-level summarization level : remove MS runs which has any missing values, and then sum of original intensities, and then log transformation.
2. groupComparison : if you used summarMethod='logOfSum', groupComparison performs t-test (not linear model) between two conditions. Therefore, there is no fitted models. Then, it is hard to recognize the order of conditions as you assigned in contrast matrix in t.test function in R. Therefore, label for comparison is shown as what t-test performed in order to keep +/- for log fold change.

Hope to help to understand.

Sincerely,
- Meena

That is, in Skyline, if you go to:

I think that you will see a report in the list there that has a blank name.  You can use the "Edit List" button to rename the report.
